selected_problem: Fresh main still allowed the canonical remote-delivery merge path to send GitHub's merge PUT with only an expected head SHA. A base branch that had already moved before delivery could therefore be merged without any base-identity check, even though that drift was observable before the write side effect.

execution.route_basis: The revision-aware truth-boundary portfolio contains several equally severe open integration boundaries, so the committed four-mode router observes high portfolio/artifact pressure and routes the source-contract replay to WHOLE_ARTIFACT rather than forcing a mode rotation.

changes: The existing GitHub delivery implementation is preserved byte-for-byte as core/git-base.mjs and reused behind a small integrity veneer rather than reimplemented.
Canonical gitRemoteDelivery merge now binds delivery to an expected base identity, deriving it from the local base ref when the caller does not supply one.
Before any push, PR-create, or merge write side effect in a merge-bearing delivery, the provider reads the remote base ref and fails closed on observable base drift.
Immediately before the merge PUT, the provider reads the pull request and verifies its reported base SHA against the same expected base identity.
The existing GitHub merge expected-head SHA precondition remains active.

validation.pre_fix_reproduction: REPRODUCED: legacy provider returned ok=true and issued PUT /pulls/9/merge without reading any base identity even when expectedBaseSha was supplied.

truth_boundaries: UNRESOLVED: direct githubMergePullRequest calls that omit expectedBaseSha still delegate to the legacy head-only helper for compatibility; the canonical gitRemoteDelivery merge path is base-bound.

BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: GitHub's merge REST endpoint still offers an atomic expected-head precondition but no equivalent caller-supplied expected-base precondition; the new GET-to-PUT base checks detect pre-existing drift but cannot eliminate a race inside the external service boundary.
No force push, repository-rule bypass, credential exposure, payment, formal Release, or destructive/irreversible action is introduced.
